OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN : Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to 
the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram,  a former Member, Shri Korambayil 
Ahammed Haji, a sitting Member, Sh ri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan, Shri 
Indradeep Sinha, former Members, Shri Bhagatram Manhar, a sitting 
Member, Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan, a former Member of this 
House. 
Shri Kishori Ram passed away on the 4th February, 2003, at the age 
of 83 years. 
Born at Village Chakand,  District Gaya, Bihar in January,  1921, 
Shri Kishori Ram had his education  at vldwat Sahitya Sammelan, Aligarh. A 
businessman by profession, Shri Kishori Ram was associated with various 
social and welfare organisations.   He devoted his life for the   uplift of tne 
downtrodden. 
Shri Kishori Ram represented the State of Bihar in this House for 
two consecutive terms from April, 1952 to April, 1956 and again from April, 
1956 to April, 1962. 
In the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram the country has lost a 
noted social worker. 
Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji passed away on the 12th May, 
2003, at the age of 72 years. 
Born at Manjeri, Kerala in June, 1931, Shri Haji had his education at 
Government Boys High School, Manjeri. A Businessman and Planter by 
profession, Shri Haji wa s associated with vari ous social, cultural and 
philanthropic activities. He served as the Director, Kerala Tourism 
Development Corporation. Shri Haji was a sports lover.   He was the founder 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July, 2003] 
President of the Malappuram District Football Association and had also 
served as the Vice-President of the Kerala Football Association. From 1998 
till his death, Shri Haji served as the General Secretary of the Indian Union 
Muslim League, Kerala. 
Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji star ted his legislative career as a 
Member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly in 1977 and remained its 
Member till 1991. Shri Haji was also elected, Deputy Speaker, Kerala 
Legislative Assembly in 1990. He represented the State of Kerala in this 
House from April, 1998 till his death. 
In the passing away of Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji, the country 
has lost a noted social worker and a distinguished Parliamentarian. 
Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan passed away on the 20th of May, 
2003, at the age of 66 years under tragic circumstances. 
Born at village Kombukkaranendal, Tamil Nadu in May, 1937, Shri 
Kiruttinan had his education at Raja Dorai Singam Memorial College, 
Sivaganga and Pachaiyappa's College, Chennai. 
An Agriculturist by vocation, Shri Kiruttinan was an active social 
and political worker. He started social work as the Secretary of Red Cross 
Society at his native village and Kalai Valrchai Kazhagam, which does social 
work and educates the people thro ugh social dramas and cultural 
programmes. Shri Kiruttinan took keen interest in serving the poor, villagers, 
illiterates and people belonging to the lowest strata of society, including 
Harijans and those belonging to back ward classes. Shri Kiruttinan was 
arrested several times in connection with various agitations in favour of the 
people of Tamil Nadu. He was Chairman of the Panchayat Union, 
Manamadurai from 1970 to 1976 and President of the VillagePanchayat, 
Theethanpettai from 1970 to 1976. 
Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan starte d his distinguished legislative 
career with the membership of the Fourth Lok Sabha. He was re-elected to 
the Fifth Lok Sabha. Shri Kiruttinan represented the State of Tamil Nadu in 
this House from March, 1989 to April, 1990 and again from April, 1990 to 
April, 1996. Thereafter, he was elect ed to the Tamil Nadu Legislative 
Assembly in the year 1996 and remained a Member of that House till 2001. 
Shri Kiruttinan also served as the Minister of State Highways and Port in the 
Government of Tamil Nadu from 1998 to 2001. 
2 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[21 July. 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
A widely travelled person, Shri Kiruttinan was member of the 
delegation to U.N.O. in the year 1990. He was also a member of the 
Parliamentary Delegation to  West Germany in the year 1972. 
In the passing away of Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan, the country 
has lost a distinguished social worker and a noted Parliamentarian. 
Shri Indradeep Sinha passed away on the 9th of June, 2003. at the 
age of 89 years following cardiac arrest. 
Born at Shakara village in Siwan District of Bihar in July, 1914, Shri 
Sinha had his education at Shakara, Dindayalpur, Maharajganj, Goreakothi 
and Patna. 
A lecturer and journalist by vocation, Shri Sinha was Secretary of 
the Bihar State Council of the Communi st Party of India from 1962 to 1967 
and had served as the General Secretar y of the All-India Kisan Sabha since 
1973 till late nineties. Shri Sinha was also editor of the 'Hunkar', 'Janasakti' 
and 'New Age' weeklies. 
Shri Indradeep Sinha started his legislative career with the 
Membership of the Bihar Legislative Co uncil, where he was a Member from 
1964 to 1974. He also served as the Minister of Revenue in the United Front 
Government of Bihar from 1967 to 1968. As Revenue Minister, he took 
several initiatives to amel iorate the condition of the poor and downtrodden 
classes and took steps for distribution of land to the landless in the State. Shri 
Sinha represented the State of Bihar in this House for two terms from April, 
1974 to April, 1980 and again from July, 1980 to July. 1986. 
In the passing away of Shri Indradeep Sinha, the country has lost a 
veteran Parliamentarian, a crusader for the common man's cause and an able 
administrator 
Shri Bhagatram Manhar passed away on the 19th June 2003, at the 
age of 65 years, following cardiac arrest. 
Born at Village Bhikhampura, District Raigarh, Chhattisgarh in 
October, 1938, Shri Manhar had done his graduation from the College of 
Agriculture, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. An Agriculturist by vocation, Shri 
Manhar was associated with trade union activities. He worked closely with 
coalmines workers as patron of th e Rashtriya Koyala Khadan Mazdoor 
Sangh of the South-Eastern Coal Field.   He also worked for the welfare of 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July, 2003] 
the  disadvantaged  sections of society.  Shri  Mannar served  as  Director, 
Tourism of the Chhattisgarh State. 
Shri Manhar began his legislative career with the membership of the 
Fifth Lok Sabha. He represented the State of Madhya Pradesh in this House 
for two consecutive terms from April 1978 to April, 1990. He was again 
elected to represent the State of Madhy a Pradesh in April, 2000. Consequent 
upon the creation of the State of Chhattisgarh, he represented that State from 
November, 2000 till his death. 
In the passing away of Shri Bhagat ram Manhar, the country has lost 
an able Parliamentarian who took keen interest in the proceedings of the 
House. 
Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan, passed away on the 8th 
July. 2003. at the age of 86 years. 
Born at Baroda in July, 1918 Shrimati Chavan had her education at 
Indore and Mumbai. A teacher by voca tion, Shrimati Chavan was an active 
social and political worker. She devoted  her life for the cause of women, 
sports and rural development. Shrimati Chavan was founder President of the 
All India Women's Cricket Association. She was also President of the Indian 
Business and Professional Women's Association. 
Shrimati Chavan had a long and distinguished legislative career. She 
was Member of the Fifth, Sixth, Eighth and Ninth Lok Sabha. She 
represented the State of Maharashtra in this House from July, 1980 to 
December, 1984. 
In the passing away of Shrimati Chavan the country has lost an 
eminent social worker and a distinguished Parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram, Shri 
Korambayil Ahammed Haji, Shri Pasu mpon Tha Kiruttinan, Shri Indradeep 
Sinha, Shri Bhagatram Manhar,   Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan . 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the Members 
of the bereaved families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy. 
4 

[21 July, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR 
Reference to victims of earthquake in Algeria 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Honourable Memb ers, the House expresses its 
heartfelt sympathies and condolences to  the friendly people of Algeria, who 
were affected by a strong earthquake on the 21 st May, 2003. This earthquake 
caused over 2000 deaths and widespread  destruction. This House notes that 
the Government of India has committed one million US Dollars for aid in 
disaster relief to the victims of the earthquake. 
   I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
Reference to victims of train accidents and cloud burst in Himachal Pradesh 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are aware, on the 15 th 
May, 2003 three coaches of the Amr itsar bound Mumbai-Amritsar Golden 
Temple Express caught fire near Ludhiana, killing thirty-six persons, 
including women and children and injuring fifteen others. The fire broke out 
within ten minutes of the train leaving the Ludhiana station and three coaches 
were completely destroyed and another one was partially damaged. 
In another train accident, on the 22 nd June, 2003, fifty-two persons 
lost their lives and twenty-six others got injured when the engine and first 
four coaches of the 904 Up Holiday sp ecial train from Karwar to Mumbai 
Central derailed due to falling of boulders between Vaibhavwadi-Rajapur 
Road stations in Ratnagiri region of Konkan Railway. 
Ewrther, on the 2 nd July 2003, the Golconda Express, running 
between Guntur and Secunderabad got derailed at Warangal station on 
Secunderabad Division of Southern Railways. Twenty-one persons were 
killed and twenty-two others got injured in this accident. 
Hon. Members, I also refer with utmost grief and sorrow to the 
tragic incident in which several persons are reported to have been washed 
away and many got injured due to flash flood caused by the cloudburst at 
Pulia Nullah in Garasa Valley in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh on the 16 th July, 
2003. The victims were asleep when the disaster took place. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA        [21 July, 2003] 
The entire House extends its heartf elt condolences to the affected 
families and also expresses sympathy and concern for those who had been 
injured. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these 
tragedies. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

Korambayil Ahammed Haji and Shri Bhagatram Manhar, sitting Members, 
the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Tuesday, the 22nd July, 2003.
